lead: >-
  On current festive itineraries through Brazil and Chile, the main event
  takes place in Rio de Janeiro: New Year's Eve on Copacabana or Carnival's
  Champions' Parade. Chile adds Santiago, Andean views and, on longer
  programs, the Atacama Desert. These tours differ in dates, duration
  and number of additional countries. We explain where a celebration
  is actually scheduled and where the program is ordinary sightseeing.
---

## Brazil and Chile for the holidays: what is actually included

This catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The shared feature of the current programs is that Brazil and Chile lie on the main itinerary and the journey is linked to a particular event. **The festive activities are concentrated in Brazil; a separate festival in Chile cannot be promised merely because of a thematic label.** Santiago offers travelers city sightseeing and, in some cases, the opportunity to add a winery visit.

The first question, therefore, is **which event you want to attend**. New Year's on Rio's seafront and the Champions' Parade at the Sambadrome are very different experiences. They require different arrival dates, visiting arrangements and accommodation. The country pairing without the events filter is shown in the [Brazil + Chile catalog](/multi-country/brazil_chile/), while other festive journeys across the continent are in [Events and Festivals](/interests/events-and-festivals/).

## New Year's Eve on Copacabana and a trip to Santiago

The [11-day New Year tour through Brazil, Argentina and Chile](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-11-days-2027/) lists dates of **December 30, 2026 – January 9, 2027**. The group celebrates New Year's Eve on Copacabana in Rio. The journey then takes in both sides of Iguazu Falls, Buenos Aires and [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). City excursions and flights between them are distinct stages of the trip.

There is also a [10-day New Year option](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-2027-10-days/), which, according to the published itinerary, runs from December 30 to January 8: festivities take place in Rio, followed by Iguazu, a tango show in Buenos Aires and Santiago. Even a one-day difference may affect flight convenience and rest after the festive night. Compare the specific sightseeing sequence as well as the length of the trip.

**On these itineraries, Chile is the continuation of the journey after the celebration.** Getting to know its capital and the Andes offers a change of scene, but anyone expecting a separate Chilean New Year's concert or festival needs explicit confirmation in the selected program. It is not automatically included simply because the tour appears in this themed selection.

## Rio Carnival: the Champions' Parade and the onward journey to Chile

The centerpiece of the [10-day “Champions' Parade, Tango and Wine” tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-champions-parade-10-days-2027/) is the Sambadrome in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). The Champions' Parade day is combined with city walks, Sugarloaf Mountain and Corcovado. The program then includes both sides of Iguazu Falls, a tango show with dinner in Buenos Aires and sightseeing in Santiago. A visit to the Maipo Valley wineries is offered as an optional addition in the published tour.

Unlike New Year's Eve on a public city beach, admission to the Champions' Parade is tied to a specific event and its tickets. Before booking, verify **the actual parade date, seating category, entry arrangements at the Sambadrome and ticket conditions** against the confirmed offer for the chosen tour. Carnival taking place in Rio does not mean admission to a specific parade is included in every Brazil itinerary.

The [18-day five-country itinerary with the Champions' Parade](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) proceeds through Chile, Bolivia and Peru after Rio, Iguazu and Argentina. The Chilean section adds Santiago and the Atacama region before the journey continues to Uyuni and Machu Picchu. This is an option for travelers who want to combine a major event with an extended Andean journey rather than return home immediately after Carnival.

## A short holiday trip or a major expedition across the continent

| Choice | Main focus |
|---|---|
| New Year, 10–11 days | Copacabana, Iguazu, Santiago |
| Champions' Parade, 10 days | Sambadrome, tango, Santiago |
| Carnival, 18–19 days | The celebration plus Atacama and Uyuni |

On shorter tours, flights between Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires and Santiago largely set the pace. On the extended [19-day five-country Carnival tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/), the festive program is followed by a high-altitude section through San Pedro de Atacama and Bolivia, then cultural stops in Peru. Physical readiness for altitude and sufficient time for long road journeys become important.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_brazil_argentina_chile_new_year_11_days_2027,tour_brazil_argentina_chile_champions_parade_10_days_2027,tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki_i_parad_chempionov_karnavala}}

**The themed catalog covers intersections of countries, not exclusively two-country trips.** Every tour mentioned here also includes at least Argentina. Some routes extend into Bolivia and Peru. Compare the full itinerary, rather than just the “Brazil + Chile” label in the filter.

## Planning the festive night and subsequent transfers

A festive day calls for different planning from an ordinary city tour. For New Year's on Copacabana, coordinate the route from the hotel to the waterfront, the return time and opportunities to rest. For the Champions' Parade, seating location and the journey to the Sambadrome matter. We help integrate these considerations into the program and account for onward flights; the final services and ticket arrangements depend on the specific tour.

After Rio comes [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) in many itineraries, followed by Argentina and a flight to Chile. When choosing connections, avoid an overly tight schedule immediately after a nighttime event. In Chile, the weather in [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) differs from Rio's coastal climate, and a tour that continues to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) requires clothing suitable for dry air, intense sunshine and cold high-altitude evenings.

Border crossings, document requirements and payment options depend on citizenship, mode of travel and current regulations. Check them for the actual dates and itinerary; a single journey through several countries does not imply uniform entry conditions.

## Frequently asked questions about holiday tours in Brazil and Chile

### Where do the festive events take place on these tours?

According to the published programs, New Year's Eve on Copacabana and the Champions' Parade take place in Rio de Janeiro. Chile provides a sightseeing continuation on these routes, not a second guaranteed festival event.

### Can we see the Champions' Parade and Atacama on the same trip?

Yes. The [18-day five-country program with the Champions' Parade](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) includes Chile, the Atacama region and Bolivia. It is an extended journey with additional countries and high-altitude transfers.

### Which should I choose: New Year or Carnival?

For New Year on an ocean beach, choose a program featuring Copacabana and late-December dates. For the samba schools' performances at the Sambadrome, choose a specific tour with the Champions' Parade. Verify ticket conditions and the festive program separately.

### Is there a tour covering only Brazil and Chile, without Argentina?

The matching published routes in this event-themed selection also include other countries. A strictly two-country option would require separately planning the geography and dates of a custom itinerary.

  not guarantee tastings in both countries: some itineraries include a visit
  to the Maipo Valley, others offer it separately, while some wine stops
  are actually in Argentina. We explain Ada Tours' real itineraries, tasting
  locations and the time to allow for culinary experiences.
---

## Brazil and Chile for food lovers: where wine is actually scheduled

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} in which Brazil and Chile are among the main countries and food and wine form a substantial part of the overall journey. This is **an intersection of itineraries and interests**, not a promise of identical wine experiences on opposite sides of the continent. Many suitable tours also include Argentina, where tango dinners or winery visits are planned.

There are specific choices to make. You might visit [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and Iguazu Falls and reserve a day in [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) for vineyards. Or choose a longer itinerary featuring Argentine wine, Patagonia and only a short Chilean stop. Both may appear under the same search filter, but the wine experiences and the time devoted to them are very different.

All itineraries with Brazil and Chile as main countries, regardless of culinary interests, appear in the [country combination catalog](/multi-country/brazil_chile/). For a broader choice of wine travel, explore [Food and Wine](/interests/food-and-wine/) and [culinary tours in Chile](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/chile/).

## Chile: Maipo, Casablanca and Millahue on real itineraries

Central Chile around Santiago is the most important area for the wine stage. The [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) is known for vineyards at the foot of the Andes; [Casablanca](/chile/place/casablanca-valley/) is nearer the Pacific coast and is particularly associated with white wines. [Colchagua](/chile/place/colchagua-valley/) and [Millahue](/chile/place/millahue-valley/) are other winegrowing regions of central Chile. Visiting all these valleys in one short day between flights would leave very little time at each stop.

The [“Best of Brazil, Argentina and Chile” tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-brazil-argentina-chile/) includes Maipo Valley vineyards on its final sightseeing day. The program combines an introduction to Santiago, the story of winemaking and a tasting. Among the options listed here, this is the clearest confirmation of a wine experience for someone who wants to sample Chilean wine during a wider itinerary featuring Patagonia and Atacama. Check the order of the day and the flight departure time after the excursion.

On the [20-day six-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/), a Maipo winery visit with tasting is available as an **optional paid excursion** during the stay in Santiago. The same distinction applies to the [New Year journey through Brazil, Argentina and Chile](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-11-days-2027/) and the [Champions' Parade tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-champions-parade-10-days-2027/): city sightseeing is included, while Maipo wineries can be added at extra cost, subject to the minimum participant requirements. Simply including the word “wine” in a tour name does not put a tasting into the base price.

There is also a more specialized example. The [17-day private grand tour of Chile and Argentina with Iguazu](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) features a separate wine day in central Chile. Its description mentions private tastings and Millahue, as well as transfer options and wine regions. The exact wineries, some transfers and inclusion of private dinners must be agreed before travel. For such a day, compare the final itinerary and confirmed services rather than promotional labels.

For the content of individual experiences, see the [Maipo wine excursion](/chile/maipo-valley/maipo-valley-wine-tour/) and [private wine day in Millahue](/chile/millahue-valley/chile-private-wine-day-millahue/).

## The Brazilian stage: Rio's cuisine and free time

Brazilian portions of the matching routes usually focus on Rio and Iguazu. Rio offers opportunities to discover local food, including feijoada, fish and seafood dishes, street snacks, markets and cafés. That alone can justify leaving free time between excursions. However, a visit to a particular restaurant, a culinary workshop or a Brazilian wine tasting must be **explicitly listed on the chosen itinerary** before it can be counted among included services.

On most extended programs, days in Brazil are occupied with city sightseeing, Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain, followed by a flight to Iguazu. A market visit or restaurant dinner can be discussed when planning free time. Not every city lunch should automatically be turned into a separate Ada Tours culinary excursion.

This is an important difference from Chile, where some specific offers include wineries or explicitly allow travelers to purchase an additional tasting. If local food in both countries is the main interest, ask for **at least one free culinary stop in Rio** and check whether the pace in Santiago allows for a separate wine day. This arrangement can be discussed individually; it does not mean extra activities are already included in the published price.

## Choosing a tour when tastings matter more than country count

Compare the actual scheduled wine experiences, not just the total number of countries or days.

| Program | Wine component |
|---|---|
| “Best of Brazil, Argentina and Chile” | Maipo: tasting included in the program |
| Six countries in 20 days | Maipo: optional excursion |
| New Year or Champions' Parade | Maipo: optional, at extra cost |
| Private grand tour, 17 days | Separate wine day in Chile |
| “Sun, Tango, Wine and Atacama” | Drives through Casablanca; tasting needs confirmation |
| “All of Argentina,” 26 days | Wineries primarily in Argentina |

The [“Sun, Tango, Wine and Atacama” tour](/multi-country/tour/sun-tango-wine-atacama/) travels through the Casablanca area of Chile on the way toward Valparaíso and Viña del Mar. The program describes the wine region, but passing through a valley does not in itself prove that a particular day includes a cellar visit and tasting. If wine is a priority, this outing should include a confirmed stop.

The [26-day “All of Argentina” grand itinerary](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) features several substantial wine days in Argentina's Cafayate and Mendoza. The Brazilian and Chilean sections have other purposes in that case: Iguazu and Patagonia. It is a good choice for lovers of **Argentine** wine, but a misleading reference for someone seeking an extensive Chilean tasting itinerary.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_luchshee_brazilii_argentiny_i_chili,tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_source_solntse_tango_vino_i_atakama,tour_chile_argentina_private_grand_tour_17_days,tour_source_vsya_argentina}}

A dedicated wine day requires travel time, a winery visit and the tasting itself. Combining a Santiago city tour, a journey to a distant valley and a flight within one short window is possible only with a suitable schedule. We help align travel dates, city sequence and ground transfers with the selected winery visit.

## When to travel: vineyards, harvest festivals and weather

Chilean wine culture is accessible to visitors beyond grape harvest season. Wineries conduct tastings according to their own schedules, and visits must be reserved for specific dates. **Harvest in central Chile generally takes place in the Southern Hemisphere's late summer and early autumn, especially February through April**, but timing varies by valley, weather and grape variety. Do not organize a journey around a particular harvest festival without a confirmed event calendar.

This is especially relevant for New Year itineraries and Rio Carnival programs. Their dates are set by the Brazilian event, while wine in Chile is an additional experience. Those dates do not automatically coincide with a special vintage tasting or a harvest celebration.

Light clothing and rain protection are useful for walks around Rio and Iguazu in Brazil. Central Chile can have cooler evenings, while extended programs featuring Atacama and Patagonia add altitude, wind and sharp temperature changes. Someone taking a short wine-oriented trip and someone joining a major continental journey need different clothing and baggage.

## Tastings, flights and purchases: what to check in advance

The principal destinations of this country combination are not adjacent overland. Between Rio or Iguazu in Brazil and Santiago in Chile, flights are generally planned around the other countries on the chosen itinerary. Journeys including Argentina add more connections and currency changes, while a transfer day can consume almost all daylight hours. A tasting is better scheduled on a full free day rather than in the evening after an arrival of uncertain timing.

For budgeting, separate the cost of the tour itself, an independently charged wine excursion, meals outside the program and winery purchases. Brazil uses the real and Chile the Chilean peso; a trip via Argentina adds another local currency. The ability to pay with foreign or Russian-issued bank cards depends on the bank, payment network and seller. Ada Tours can discuss payment methods and alternatives in advance, but cannot guarantee that any card will work.

On entry to Chile, plant and animal products must be declared in accordance with the local agricultural authority SAG's rules. If you plan to bring food gifts, check their admissibility at each border. Wine bottles are also subject to current customs allowances and your airline's rules for carrying liquids in baggage. Do not assume the same purchasing and transport rules apply throughout the route.

Passport and visa requirements must be checked **against each traveler's nationality and exact dates**. Permission to enter one country does not automatically cover another. When planning an individual trip, we can clarify the travel sequence, transit-document requirements and time needed for border procedures in advance.

## Frequently asked questions about food and wine journeys through Brazil and Chile

### Are Chilean wine tastings included on every tour in this selection?

No. The “Best of Brazil, Argentina and Chile” program includes a Maipo tasting, while New Year and Carnival options list Maipo wineries as an additional excursion. On other journeys, the wine theme may primarily concern Argentina.

### Can we combine Rio's cuisine and Chile's vineyards in one journey?

Yes. Choose an itinerary including Rio and Santiago, then check the free time available in Brazil and whether a confirmed wine day is scheduled in Chile. Restaurant visits and tastings must either be listed on the itinerary or arranged as extra services.

### Is one day in the Maipo Valley enough?

For a single winery excursion from Santiago, it is a realistic format with a prearranged schedule. Comparing several wineries across different valleys requires more time, especially when the itinerary already includes distant flights.

### Are any of these offers standalone trips exclusively through Brazil and Chile?

The catalog title means that both countries feature on the main itinerary. Most listed programs also cover Argentina and sometimes other nations. Check the full country list on each [itinerary in this selection](/multi-country/brazil_chile/).

### When is the best time for a grape harvest festival?

Harvest celebrations in central Chile are generally associated with late summer and early autumn, but exact event dates are confirmed annually. If a festival is the priority, start with its confirmed date and wine region, then plan the Brazil section and the other countries.

  Nature journeys through Brazil and Chile connect very different climate zones:
  Iguazu Falls and the Atlantic coast with the dry Atacama or Patagonia's
  glaciers. We explain which combinations really appear in current routes,
  why travel often passes through Argentina and what to consider when

## Nature in Brazil and Chile: from Iguazu to Atacama and Patagonia

Brazil and Chile are compelling to combine precisely because of their different natural environments. Brazil offers the humid subtropical scenery of [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and the green hills of the Atlantic coast. Chilean routes may take you north to the dry high-altitude landscapes of [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), or south to Patagonia's mountains and glaciers.

But the words “Brazil and Chile” do not reveal the full itinerary. Many of our nature-focused tours also pass through Argentina, including Buenos Aires, the Argentine side of Iguazu, glaciers or transit stops between regions. First decide which natural contrast you want to experience, then examine the country list and the day-by-day itinerary.

## Three ways to combine natural experiences

### Waterfalls and the Atacama Desert

The 15-day [“Sun, Tango, Wine and Atacama”](/multi-country/tour/sun-tango-wine-atacama/) combines Rio de Janeiro, Iguazu, Buenos Aires, Santiago and San Pedro de Atacama. The focus shifts from water, tropical vegetation and Rio's scenic viewpoints to the desert expanses, rocks and highlands of northern Chile.

Choose this option for changing landscapes, but it is not a journey into southern Patagonia. Find out how much time is devoted to Atacama's natural sites and how much to cities, wine and cultural stops. Simply staying in San Pedro does not mean every possible astronomy or high-altitude excursion in the region is included in the price.

### Iguazu, glaciers and Torres del Paine

The 15-day [“Chile–Argentina–Brazil”](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-brazil/) route passes through Santiago, Puerto Natales, El Calafate, Buenos Aires, Iguazu and Rio de Janeiro. In Chile, travelers see [Torres del Paine National Park](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/); in Argentina, [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/); and toward the end of the journey, the falls on the Argentina–Brazil border.

This itinerary offers an especially dramatic change in scenery: wind and ice in the south, then powerful waterfalls and lush subtropical vegetation. Such diversity comes at the cost of long journeys between regions. Compare not just the number of attractions but the days taken up by transfers and flights.

### An extended route through several natural environments

The 13-day [“Best of Brazil, Argentina and Chile”](/multi-country/tour/best-of-brazil-argentina-chile/) program includes Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires, Patagonia's glaciers, Torres del Paine, Santiago and Atacama. It is a packed itinerary, and its total duration limits the time between distant natural areas. Read each stage's schedule carefully if you want relaxed walks, photography and flexibility to reschedule activities due to weather.

| Priority | What to compare |
|---|---|
| Water and desert | Iguazu + Atacama |
| Waterfalls and ice | Iguazu + Patagonia |
| The widest range of landscapes | Extended three-country journey |

## Why Argentina often appears between Brazil and Chile

Brazil and Chile do not share a land border. When a journey links their natural attractions with stops in Argentina, this is a genuine three-country trip, not just a formal connection. Iguazu makes that particularly clear: the Brazilian and Argentine sides of the falls are separate visiting areas with different views and entrances.

On Patagonia itineraries, the Argentine section may be needed to visit Perito Moreno and El Calafate; routes toward Atacama follow a different geography. Two tours featuring the same three countries do not necessarily have the same roads, excursions or border crossings.

Compare [all tours through Brazil and Chile](/multi-country/brazil_chile/) and [Brazil's nature tours](/interests/nature/tours/brazil/) with [Chile's nature routes](/interests/nature/tours/chile/). If Patagonia alone is your interest, a [combination of Argentina and Chile](/multi-country/argentina_chile/interests/nature/) may offer more time in the south.

## Seasons: one calendar, two different climates

Brazil's tropical and subtropical areas and Chile's high-altitude or Patagonian regions cannot be judged by a single “best month.” At Iguazu, water volume and walking conditions depend on rain and weather. In Atacama, dry air and considerable altitude on some excursions combine with cold nights. In Patagonia, the Southern Hemisphere's warm season brings longer daylight hours, but strong winds and changing weather remain common.

When choosing dates, decide which natural attraction is your main reason for traveling. For Torres del Paine, access to your preferred park trails matters most. For Atacama, look at the mountain-excursion schedule and acclimatization time. Iguazu can be combined with different itineraries more easily, but visits to both national parks on either side of the border should be checked against the actual program.

## Flights, altitude and baggage

The contrasting climates call for thoughtful packing: lightweight clothes for Brazil's hot areas, windproof and waterproof layers for Patagonia, or warm clothing for the Chilean highlands. Numerous flights add baggage limits and connection time. Read the daily itinerary alongside the list of included and excluded flights rather than assume every flight is part of every package.

Some Atacama excursions climb considerably higher than San Pedro. Travelers should discuss their tolerance for altitude and the physical demands of the specific activities in advance. In Patagonia, the required fitness depends on whether the activity is sightseeing, trekking or walking on ice.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Brazil and Chile

### Can we see Iguazu and Atacama on the same trip?

Yes. These regions are connected, for example, by the [15-day “Sun, Tango, Wine and Atacama” route](/multi-country/tour/sun-tango-wine-atacama/), which also visits Argentina.

### Does a Brazil-and-Chile itinerary include Patagonia's glaciers?

Not necessarily. There is an option featuring Torres del Paine and Perito Moreno, but other tours focus on northern Chile or city stops. Check the actual program.

### Is there a shared border crossing between Brazil and Chile?

No, these countries do not border each other. Depending on the chosen route, flights and/or overland sections through other countries, including Argentina, are used.

### How does nature travel differ from safaris and wildlife watching?

Here the main experiences are landscapes, waterfalls, mountains and natural areas. If observing animals is the priority, explore the separate [“Wildlife and Safaris” selection](/interests/wildlife/) and the confirmed activities on each tour.

## Wildlife and safaris in Brazil and Chile: what the itineraries contain

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Most programs also travel through Argentina and other South American countries, so the “Brazil and Chile” filter **does not mean a direct flight between those two countries**. The “Wildlife and Safaris” label applies to the entire journey: actual animal watching may take place in only one of several countries.

In Brazil, a main natural attraction is [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). In Chile, travelers can choose between [Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), with salt flats and lagoons, and [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/), with lakes, steppe and mountain valleys. These are very different natural environments, so the main goal of the journey should guide the choice of route.

## The Brazilian section: Iguazu and Atlantic Forest

[Iguazu National Park](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) preserves a large section of Atlantic Forest with rich plant and animal life. Rare species, including jaguars, inhabit the area, but their presence does not mean visitors will see them from a sightseeing trail. A standard waterfalls excursion focuses on the cascades, panoramic views and forest surroundings. Specialized wildlife watching is not automatically included.

On the [“Best of Brazil, Argentina and Chile”](/multi-country/tour/best-of-brazil-argentina-chile/), the Brazilian stop at Iguazu is combined with a separate visit to the Argentine side, Buenos Aires and Chilean natural areas. The two sides of the falls are in different countries and have separate visiting rules. Travelers interested in forest ecosystems should check how much time is spent inside the parks and how much on borders and transfers.

The [“Best of Brazil, Argentina and Chile”](/multi-country/tour/best-of-brazil-argentina-chile/) belongs to the [“Nature” interest](/interests/nature/), but is not tagged as a “Wildlife and Safaris” tour. If wildlife is the reason for traveling, compare current [tours including Brazil and animal watching](/interests/wildlife/tours/brazil/): a waterfall sightseeing trip is not, by itself, birdwatching or a safari.

## Chile: Atacama or Patagonia

On the [“Sun, Tango, Wine and Atacama” tour](/multi-country/tour/sun-tango-wine-atacama/), the Chilean stage after Rio, Iguazu and Argentina includes high-altitude lagoons, the Socaire area, the Atacama Salt Flat and the El Tatio geysers. The itinerary features Chaxa Lagoon in a flamingo reserve, with an opportunity to see these birds. On the return from El Tatio, it also mentions opportunities to watch vicuñas and viscachas. Actual encounters depend on conditions and are not guaranteed.

[Los Flamencos National Reserve](/chile/place/los-flamencos-national-reserve/) protects natural areas around Atacama. Access to particular lagoons and roads depends on the weather, and conditions for visiting each sector should be confirmed before departure. Early starts, dry air and substantial altitude call for warm clothing and a sensible pace.

For comparison of landscapes, [“Best of Brazil, Argentina and Chile”](/multi-country/tour/best-of-brazil-argentina-chile/) includes [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) with lakes and mountain panoramas. Guanacos, condors and other birds inhabit the park, but the tour does not list specialized viewing of these species. The itinerary appears in [Chile's “Nature” catalog](/interests/nature/tours/chile/), rather than in the safari selection.

## Which itineraries actually carry the “Wildlife and Safaris” tag

| Program | Where wildlife watching features in the full itinerary |
|---|---|
| [“Sun, Tango, Wine and Atacama”](/multi-country/tour/sun-tango-wine-atacama/) | Chile: Chaxa Lagoon flamingos; vicuñas and viscachas on the return from El Tatio |
| [“Eight South American Countries in 32 Days”](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) | Bolivia: flamingos at Laguna Colorada; Ecuador: an alternative Galápagos excursion with birds and marine wildlife |

On the second tour, the main wildlife experiences take place in Bolivia and Ecuador, **outside the selected Brazil + Chile pair**. ## Climate, flights and pace

Iguazu has a humid subtropical climate; Atacama is a dry high-altitude desert; and Patagonia is colder and windier. Combining these regions requires light clothes for warm areas, sun protection, closed shoes, insulating layers and a windproof or waterproof outer layer. An average weather forecast “for Chile” is of little use here: check the actual regions and dates.

Transfers may go through Buenos Aires and other intermediate cities. Allowing some time for poor weather is useful for park walks and wildlife watching, and acclimatization matters for high-altitude stops. We help coordinate the order of visits, domestic flights, sightseeing schedule and current park rules. If the goal is to see certain birds or animals, that wish should be matched to the actual excursions, not just to a thematic heading.

## Frequently asked questions about wildlife in Brazil and Chile

### Can I see a jaguar on an Iguazu excursion?

A sighting cannot be guaranteed. Jaguars live in the protected forest, but a sightseeing excursion to the waterfalls is not a specialized program for observing large predators.

### Which is better for birds and lagoons: Atacama or Patagonia?

The [“Sun, Tango, Wine and Atacama” tour](/multi-country/tour/sun-tango-wine-atacama/) includes Chaxa Lagoon and its flamingos, plus the road back from El Tatio where vicuñas and viscachas may be spotted. [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) offers steppe and mountain scenery, but the mentioned “Best of Brazil, Argentina and Chile” tour does not include a separate safari.

### Does the journey have to cover only Brazil and Chile?

No. The selection also contains itineraries with other main countries, such as Argentina. The full list of countries and border crossings appears on each tour page.

### What matters most when visiting high-altitude lagoons?

Altitude, cold early-morning conditions and possible road closures. Check access, the pace of ascent and any personal medical restrictions before traveling, rather than relying on Rio's coastal climate.

## Brazil, Chile and Colombia: three countries with very different experiences

[Brazil](/brazil/), [Chile](/chile/) and [Colombia](/colombia/) form an unusual combination: Atlantic shores and immense waterfalls, dry Andean landscapes, historic neighborhoods and the Caribbean coast. Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with these countries among the main sections of the itinerary.

**An important clarification:** on the [eight-country South America tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) under consideration, the selected countries are not visited consecutively. After Brazil, travelers visit Argentina and Uruguay; Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador follow Chile's Atacama; only then does the Colombian stage begin. This selection must not be understood as a standalone Rio–Santiago–Cartagena itinerary, with direct connections between the three selected nations.

| Country | What the program includes |
|---|---|
| Brazil | Rio, Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain, Iguazu |
| Chile | Santiago, Calama, San Pedro de Atacama |
| Colombia | Medellín, Guatapé, Cartagena, Bogotá |

The combination suits a long journey featuring varied cultural and natural stops. For a shorter holiday, compare separate [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/), [Chile tours](/chile/tour/) and [Colombia tours](/colombia/tour/): each extra international connection reduces the time available in any particular city.

## Brazil: Rio first, then Iguazu Falls

The Brazilian section starts with arrival in São Paulo and a flight to [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). The city program includes Corcovado with Christ the Redeemer, Sugarloaf Mountain and a walk through historic districts. Visits to the main viewpoints are described as group excursions with a Russian-speaking guide. A substantial budget for a multi-country journey **does not therefore mean every excursion is private**.

Travelers then fly to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The Brazilian side of the waterfalls is scheduled here, followed by the Argentine side and the next section of the route. Each side requires time and an actual crossing of the international border. The Bird Park and Macuco Safari are optional, separately payable activities on the stated program; they must not be treated as mandatory included services.

**What matters when choosing:** Rio and Iguazu combine a major city, ocean coastline and a powerful natural attraction, but a proper beach holiday requires checking the number of free days. On the described itinerary, city sightseeing is followed by flights rather than a long stay at a beach resort.

## Chile: the capital and Atacama, not Patagonia

The Chilean section starts with a flight from Buenos Aires to [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). A sightseeing tour with a Russian-speaking guide covers the historic center, the La Moneda Palace area, Plaza de Armas and Santa Lucía Hill. A visit to Maipo Valley wineries is offered separately for an additional fee.

Next, the route flies to Calama and continues by road to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This is an important preparation stage before the subsequent high-altitude journey through Bolivia. An evening astronomy excursion with telescopes is offered **on request**, rather than automatically included.

Some travelers see “Chile” in a selection and expect Torres del Paine, glaciers or the long trails of Patagonia. **This program covers different parts of Chile:** Santiago and the northern Atacama. If Chilean Patagonia is the goal, choose a route with confirmed stops in the south, for instance via the [general Chile tour catalog](/chile/tour/), and check the length of any hiking activities separately.

Visiting Atacama involves dry air, intense sunshine, cold nights and wide temperature swings. Accommodation and transport conditions change after the capital, and the following section across the Bolivian border lies at high altitude. According to the program, some stages exceed 4000 m. Acclimatization and medical assessment of risks are important even for travelers primarily interested in the cities of Brazil and Colombia.

## Colombia: three cities and distinct urban experiences

After Ecuador, the program includes a flight from Guayaquil to [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). Near the city, a visit to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and the El Peñón rock is planned. The next day introduces [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/), followed by a flight to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/).

Cartagena reveals a different Colombia: a historic port city with colonial architecture and a Caribbean coastline. A city excursion is planned here before the journey continues to [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/). The capital's program includes museums, Monserrate and an excursion to the Salt Cathedral at Zipaquirá. Check the detailed itinerary for the actual duration of walks and guiding languages.

This part of the route has **three different urban environments**. Medellín is associated with mountainous terrain and outings to nearby towns; Cartagena has a humid coastal climate and a historic port; Bogotá is a high-altitude capital. The clothing required and how you feel may vary between them, even though they are in one country.

Distinguish what is actually included from popular associations. A visit to Colombia does not mean the tour includes the Amazon rainforest, coffee plantations or a multi-day island beach resort. The itinerary in question focuses on Medellín, Guatapé, Cartagena, Bogotá and Zipaquirá. Travelers interested in a specialized cultural route can review [cultural tours in Colombia](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/colombia/) and compare the day-by-day activities.

## Logistics between the three selected countries

Since Brazil, Chile and Colombia are parts of a much longer journey here, **planning only three flights would be a mistake**. The complete geography also includes Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador. The route features flights, a one-day ferry excursion, road transfers and high-altitude sections.

On an extended journey, the key question is less about the number of borders than the time left to visit specific attractions. A full sightseeing day does not automatically begin immediately after a flight and transfer into Rio. Similarly, flying to Calama, checking in at San Pedro and preparing for Bolivia take a separate day; flights between Colombian cities also require airport and baggage time.

| Section | Main consideration |
|---|---|
| Rio – Iguazu | Flight and both sides of the border |
| Santiago – Atacama | Flight to Calama, transfer, altitude |
| Medellín – Cartagena – Bogotá | Domestic flights and time for sightseeing |

We help coordinate flights and road transfers, allow sensible connection buffers and prepare a document checklist based on the traveler's citizenship. Final airline and immigration requirements and actual connecting times must nevertheless be checked for the specific flights and dates. On this itinerary, moving one long-distance section may affect the entire subsequent chain of hotels and excursions.

## Weather and baggage: three contrasting climate scenarios

**Rio** calls for clothing suitable for warm, humid weather and protection against sun and rain. **Atacama** calls for layers to handle cool mornings and nights alongside intense daytime sunshine; entering Bolivia adds true high-altitude conditions. **Cartagena** can be hot and humid, while **Bogotá** is considerably cooler because of its elevation.

One bag full of summer clothes is therefore not enough for the whole journey. Divide your clothes into small sets for city walks, flights, desert and highlands, and the humid coast. Check baggage allowances against the most restrictive domestic flight on the complete itinerary, not just the international ticket.

There is no single month that is “ideal for all three countries.” At Iguazu, water levels and park conditions affect the accessibility of some trails; for Atacama and Altiplano crossings, high-altitude weather and road conditions matter; on Colombia's Caribbean coast, rain and humidity vary seasonally. Choose dates according to your main objective and confirm which excursions can actually operate in that period.

## Documents, health and money

The selected trio, like the full tour, involves different tourist entry regulations. For [Brazil](/brazil/), [Chile](/chile/) and [Colombia](/colombia/), advance-entry requirements depend on citizenship and trip type; all intermediate countries must also be considered. Colombia's Check-Mig pre-registration system is described by migration authorities as voluntary, but its current procedures should be checked before flying. Visa-free access to one country does not establish entry rights to the others.

Health considerations extend beyond heat. Travel through the Bolivian highlands and the later visit to high-altitude Bogotá call for attention to personal altitude tolerance. Insurance coverage and medical limitations should be checked for active excursions and transfers. A physician can advise on the risks of the high-altitude section and preventive measures appropriate to the regions visited.

The journey requires **Brazilian reais, Chilean pesos and Colombian pesos** at different stages. Currency exchange and acceptance vary by country and type of purchase. Check payment methods for hotels, optional excursions and local services. Visa and Mastercard cards issued by Russian banks do not work for international payments; cards from other issuers depend on the bank and merchant. The reliable approach is to verify both a main and backup payment method instead of relying on one universal card.

## Frequently asked questions about Brazil, Chile and Colombia tours

### Is there a ready-made itinerary covering only these three countries?

The selection shows tours where all three countries are among the main stops. The itinerary under discussion covers eight countries and includes substantial stages between them. A journey limited strictly to Brazil, Chile and Colombia would require separately agreeing on a different route.

### Does the Chilean portion include Patagonia?

Not on the described itinerary. It includes Santiago and San Pedro de Atacama, after which travelers continue to Bolivia. To see Patagonia, choose a tour featuring specific southern regions and national parks.

### Is the Atacama astronomy excursion included?

It is offered as an optional evening excursion. Its conditions and availability depend on the date; it is not automatically included.

### Can all the Colombian days be spent in Cartagena?

Not on this itinerary. The Colombian section includes Medellín, Guatapé, Cartagena, Bogotá and Zipaquirá. For a holiday focused primarily on the Caribbean coast, choose a different pace and distribution of overnight stays.

### Is this journey suitable without specialized mountain training?

Most city excursions require no athletic qualifications, but the complete route includes high-altitude stages in Bolivia above 4000 m. Altitude tolerance does not depend on fitness alone; assess acclimatization and medical contraindications in advance.
